source: Internet Archive djen-tjro-2025 OCR cadernos (public DJEN publications) for the original 20-doc seed; TJRO JURIS system (src/tjro_juris, real digitally-native court text, not OCR) for the 20-doc expansion batch, the 20-doc preliminar-targeted Round A batch, the 20-doc costs/fees-targeted Round B batch, and the 18-doc general-volume Round C batch
per_class_note: Counts above are train-split only, matching the original convention. Round C (18 general-purpose SENTENCA docs, no category-specific pre-filter, general volume push) added 12 more spans/doc on average across most categories but contributed ZERO new honorarios_fim -- confirming Round B's finding: a clean, separate honorarios_fim closing is genuinely rare in this corpus (Juizado Especial boilerplate overwhelmingly fuses custas+honorarios with no separable close). honorarios_fim=6 in train remains the only open G2 gap; closing it needs another deliberately-targeted round (e.g. homologacao-de-acordo sentencas, which is where Round B's 2 honorarios_fim examples both came from), not more general sampling.
labeler: prompt_subagents:haiku (original 20-doc seed, one labeling subagent per batch, acordaos first); prompt_subagents:general-purpose, one per document, for the 20-doc JURIS expansion batch, the 20-doc Round A preliminar-targeted batch, the 20-doc Round B costs/fees-targeted batch, and the 18-doc Round C general-volume batch
verification_note: IMPORTANT provenance distinction: the original 20-doc seed's val+test went through a decorrelated 4-role Sonnet ensemble verification pass before being trusted as eval-quality gold. The 20-doc JURIS expansion batch, the 20-doc Round A preliminar-targeted batch (tjro_juris_acordao_prelim_*), the 20-doc Round B costs/fees-targeted batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_costs_*), and the 18-doc Round C general-volume batch (tjro_juris_sentenca_vol_*) have NOT gone through that ensemble verification -- each has single-subagent labeling (one general-purpose agent per document, each independently briefed with the full annotation guideline), mechanical validation (opf_annotate.py validate: 0 offset/overlap/label-space errors across all splits), and a manual spot-check of a sample of records by the orchestrating session (not exhaustive, not the full ensemble). Treat val/test docs from these batches as provisional-quality until they receive the same ensemble verification pass the original seed used, especially before reporting any eval metric that includes them.
notes: Seed gold built the subagent way: strict sampling (acordao requires ACORDAO+VOTO+ACORDAM, sentenca requires SENTENCA+dispositivo-formula+operative-verb; despachos excluded), Haiku labeling subagents returning {category,match,nth}, offsets resolved by opf_annotate from-spans, overlaps removed deterministically, then a decorrelated 4-role Sonnet ensemble over val+test. ref_normativa was originally excluded (regex pre-pass at inference) but was added back to the trained label space and bootstrapped into every split via the same regex pre-pass (scripts/ref_normativa_prepass.py) against the already-verified gold text -- see git history for the architecture decision and the regex fix (thousands-separator article numbers, spelled-out inciso/paragrafo/alinea) that preceded it. A second real bug was found and fixed in scripts/ref_normativa_prepass.py's merge_with_opf_spans: it only reliably favored a gold/model span over an overlapping regex span on an exact start-position tie, not on the more common case of a regex match starting earlier but still partially overlapping -- a real gold custas_fim span was being silently dropped by this before the fix. 20-doc JURIS expansion batch added 2026-07-16 (see verification_note above) via the same subagent-labeling + opf_annotate.py from-spans/validate pipeline as the original seed, sourced from src/tjro_juris rather than DJEN cadernos. A follow-up 20-doc Round A batch (also 2026-07-16) closed the preliminar_inicio/fim zero-support gap: candidates were pre-filtered from TJRO JURIS's 2024-08-ACORDAO.parquet for a literal '\\b1\\.\\s*PRELIMINARES?\\b' numbered-heading match (found via manual audit that this heading convention is real but recent -- zero hits in 2005/2008/2017 samples, 21 hits in 2024-08 alone), then subagent-labeled the same way; all 20 confirmed a genuine preliminar section, split 14/3/3 train/val/test (seed 771). A follow-up 20-doc Round B batch (also 2026-07-16) targeted custas_fim/honorarios_fim/fundamentacao_legal: candidates were pre-filtered from TJRO JURIS's 2022-02-SENTENCA.parquet for both 'custas' and 'honorarios' substring mentions (excluding the 10 sentenca ids already used in the earlier expansion batch); several subagents independently anchored custas and honorarios on the exact same fused-clause span (a genuine ambiguity in Juizado Especial boilerplate, not an agent error -- the guideline explicitly allowed it), which opf_annotate validate correctly rejected as BIOES overlaps; 13 such conflicts were resolved deterministically by keeping the first-listed span and dropping the duplicate, then the batch was split 14/3/3 with a hand-picked (not random) val/test doc selection to guarantee each weak category met its per-split minimum despite the tiny (5-20 doc) supply for some categories. An 18-doc Round C batch (also 2026-07-16) pulled a fresh, unfiltered SENTENCA sample from TJRO JURIS's 2020-10-SENTENCA.parquet (a file not used by any prior batch) purely for G5 volume, split 12/3/3 (random, seed 773) -- it produced zero new honorarios_fim (see per_class_note), a real finding about how rare that specific closing shape is, not a labeling gap. Single-tribunal (TJRO) corpus of 98 docs; still needs a deliberately-targeted (not general) round to close the last G2 gap (honorarios_fim=6/10 in train) and ~52 more docs overall for G5 (>=150 total); G4 multi-tribunal remains waived for the first training checkpoint per explicit user direction.
